summary: Yuanying Shi (1878–1953) specialized in Buddhist and religious studies, studying under teachers including Tongzhi, Zengxi, Miaolian, Yekai, Bazhi Toutuo, and Dagong Heshang. He served as abbot at Jiedai, Tiantong, and Yongquan temples, and held leadership roles in the Buddhist Association of China.

Yudru Tsomu is a scholar of Tibetology and history/archaeology. She earned her PhD at Harvard University under doctoral supervisor Leonard van der Kuijp, advisors Mark Elliott, Janet Gyatso, and Philip A. Kuhn, and teachers James E. Bosson, Wesley M. Jacobsen, and Kent Buys.

Yuen Ren Chao (1892–1982) was a scholar in linguistics and sinology. He studied at Tsinghua (~1909–1910), Cornell (1910–1914), and Harvard (1915–1918), and later held posts at Cornell (~1919–1920), Harvard (~1921–1924), Tsinghua (~1925–1929), and UC Berkeley (~1947–1963).
Yuexia (1858–1917) was a scholar in Buddhist studies who founded Huayan University and served there as a teacher.

Yuguang Liu works in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He studied at Northwest Minzu University in 2000 under Bsam gtan, Tashi Tsering, Gongbaojie, and Gyalog, and completed a PhD at Hong Kong University of Science and Technology (attested 2005).
Yuhiko Katsuzaki (born 1946) is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Taisho University and later served as its president from circa 2011 to 2013.
Yui Chi Lau (1914–1997) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology who studied under traditional teacher Yingguang Qu and founded the Hong Kong Vajrayana Esoteric Society.

Yui Suzuki works in Japanology, Buddhist studies, and history/archaeology. Suzuki completed a doctorate at the University of California, Los Angeles, supervised by William M. Bodiford, Lothar von Falkenhausen, and Donald F. McCallum, and was affiliated with the University of Maryland, College Park (attested 2012).

Yuichi Kajiyama (1925–2004) studied Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Indology at Kyoto University, Nava Nalanda Mahavihara, SOAS, and Vienna under scholars including Satkari Mookerjee, J. Kashab, John Brough, and Erich Frauwallner. He held posts at Kyoto University, Bukkyo University, and Soka University.

Yuichi Shionoya (1932–2015) was a scholar of philosophy who studied at Nagoya University (~1951–1953) and Hitotsubashi University (~1953–1958). He subsequently held an academic post at Nagoya University from circa 1963 to 1973.

Yuishin Ito (1931–2023) specialized in Buddhist studies, earning degrees from Bukkyo University and studying at Doshisha University. He held positions at Bukkyo University (1961–1997), Kyoto Bunkyo Junior College, Kyoto Bunkyo Gakuen, Shōjōke-in Temple, and Chion-in Temple.

Yujiro Motora (1858–1912) worked in philosophy, having studied at Johns Hopkins University in 1885. He held posts at Tokyo University of Education (~1888–1898) and the University of Tokyo (~1888–1912).
Yujun Endo (1939–2017) was a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology who held posts at Taisho University, including associate professor (attested 1991) and professor emeritus (attested 2014).
Yuka Otani is a Buddhist studies scholar who held posts as a part-time lecturer at Ryukoku University and Hanazono University (both attested 2015).

Yukei Matsunaga (1929–2023) studied Buddhist studies and Tibetology at Koyasan University, Tohoku University, and Kyushu University. He later served as director at Koyasan University (1983) and held a post at Shuchiin University (~1999–2006).
Yuki Takatsukasa is a Buddhist studies scholar who pursued doctoral studies at Kyoto University (attested 2015) and served there as a part-time lecturer (attested 2017).

Yukihiko Asayama is a scholar of Buddhist studies and history/archaeology. He held a professorship at Hokkaido University of Education (attested 1986) and served as a Ministry of Education overseas researcher at South China Normal University (attested 1991).

Yukihiro Okada specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at the University of Tokyo (attested 1981) and under Michael Hahn (attested 1987), later serving as associate professor (attested 1996) and professor emeritus (attested 2015) at Kobe Women's University Seto Junior College.

Yukihisa Yamao (1935–2021) specialized in history, archaeology, and Japanology. He studied at Ritsumeikan University from circa 1954 to 1963 and subsequently held an academic post there from circa 1968 to 2000.
Yukio Hattori (1932–2007) was a scholar in Japanology and history/archaeology who studied at Nagoya University and held a post at Japan Women's University.
